vocabulary.definition: Rules that let you reorder or regroup numbers without changing an expression's value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reglas que permiten reordenar o reagrupar números sin cambiar el valor de una expresión.
vocabulary.cloze: Rules that let you reorder or regroup without changing the ___.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the order and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar el orden y obtener la misma respuesta.
vocabulary.visual: 3 + 7 = 7 + 3 = 10 both ways; 4 × 5 = 5 × 4 = 20 both ways — order does not matter
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that order does not change a sum or product, like a + b = b + a, is the ___.

examples.why: Changing the order keeps the same sum.
That shows the associative property, which regroups.

vocabulary.definition: You can change the grouping and get the same answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puedes cambiar la agrupación y obtener la misma respuesta.
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that grouping does not change a sum or product, like (a + b) + c = a + (b + c), is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: Adding 0 or multiplying by 1 keeps the same value.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar 0 o multiplicar por 1 mantiene el mismo valor.
vocabulary.visual: 9 + 0 = 9 (zero is the identity for addition); 6 × 1 = 6 (one is the identity for multiplication)
vocabulary.cloze: The rule that adding 0 or multiplying by 1 keeps a number the same is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: A rule that is always true in math.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla que siempre es verdadera en matemáticas.
vocabulary.visual: Commutative works for + and ×, but NOT for − or ÷ (since 5 − 3 = 2 but 3 − 5 = −2)
vocabulary.cloze: A rule that is always true in math is a ___.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Multiplicar un número por todo lo que está dentro del paréntesis: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Vintage Comic Books
revealWordProblem.text:
Diamond wants to buy vintage comic books from an online retailer. The price of a comic book depends on its condition, as shown. She plans to buy some in good condition and some in near mint condition, plus a protective cover for $0.50 for each comic book. The retailer charges $9.99 for shipping. She is deciding among three combinations: three near mint and two good; two near mint and six good; one near mint and ten good.
Question: How could Diamond use an algebraic expression to find and compare the cost of different numbers of good and near mint comic books? Which combination would you recommend she buy?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A price table for vintage comic books by condition: Poor $0.50, Fair $2.50, Good $5.50, Very Fine $10.00, Near Mint $20.00.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Let g be the number of good comics and n the number of near mint comics. Good books cost $5.50 each and near mint $20.00 each, every book needs a $0.50 cover, and shipping is $9.99 once: total = 5.50g + 20n + 0.50(g + n) + 9.99, which simplifies to 6g + 20.50n + 9.99. Now substitute each combination. Three near mint and two good: 6(2) + 20.50(3) + 9.99 = $83.49 for 5 books. Two near mint and six good: 6(6) + 20.50(2) + 9.99 = $86.99 for 8 books. One near mint and ten good: 6(10) + 20.50(1) + 9.99 = $90.49 for 11 books. The last combination costs the most in total but the least per book, so I would recommend it if Diamond wants the most comics for her money.

questions.explanation: The order of the addends changed, so this is the Commutative Property of Addition.
choiceFeedback: That property is about regrouping numbers with parentheses. Look closely at this statement: no parentheses moved, but the two numbers traded places.
Associative changes the grouping, not the order. Commutative swaps positions.
hints: Compare the two sides: same numbers, same operation. What changed between left and right?
Match the change to the property: order swapping, regrouping with parentheses, or adding 0 / multiplying by 1.
Left is 5 + 13; right is 13 + 5. The addends traded places — find the property about changing order.
questions.explanationEs: Cambió el orden de los sumandos, así que esta es la Propiedad Conmutativa de la Suma.
hintsEs: Compara los dos lados: mismos números, misma operación. ¿Qué cambió entre la izquierda y la derecha?
Une el cambio con la propiedad: cambiar el orden, reagrupar con paréntesis, o sumar 0 / multiplicar por 1.
La izquierda es 5 + 13; la derecha es 13 + 5. Los sumandos cambiaron de lugar: busca la propiedad del cambio de orden.

questions.explanation: The grouping (parentheses) changed but the order stayed the same, so this is the Associative Property of Multiplication.
choiceFeedback: That property changes the order of the numbers. Read the factors left to right on both sides — they appear as 6, 3, 2 either way, so something else must have shifted.
Only the parentheses moved. That's Associative, not Commutative (which swaps order).
The grouping changed from (6 × 3) × 2 to 6 × (3 × 2). That's Associative.
hints: Read both sides carefully: 6, 3, 2 stay in the same order. Only the parentheses moved.
Ask: did the ORDER change, or did the GROUPING change? Each property handles one of those.
Left groups (6 × 3) first; right groups (3 × 2) first. Pick the property that's about regrouping.
questions.explanationEs: La agrupación (los paréntesis) cambió pero el orden se mantuvo igual, así que esta es la Propiedad Asociativa de la Multiplicación.
hintsEs: Lee ambos lados con cuidado: 6, 3 y 2 siguen en el mismo orden. Solo se movieron los paréntesis.
Pregunta: ¿cambió el ORDEN o cambió la AGRUPACIÓN? Cada propiedad se encarga de una de esas.
La izquierda agrupa (6 × 3) primero; la derecha agrupa (3 × 2) primero. Elige la propiedad que trata de reagrupar.

questions.explanation: Adding 0 does not change the value, so this is the Identity Property of Addition.
choiceFeedback: That property is about two numbers swapping positions, and nothing swapped here. Focus instead on what adding 0 does to the value.
Zero 'does nothing' to the number — you get the same number back.
That property spreads a factor across a sum inside parentheses. There are no parentheses and no multiplication in this statement.
hints: Notice what was added: 0. Did adding it change 47 at all?
Think about what each property does. Which one is about a number staying itself?
47 + 0 gives back 47 unchanged. Find the property named for keeping a number's identity.
questions.explanationEs: Sumar 0 no cambia el valor, así que esta es la Propiedad de Identidad de la Suma.
hintsEs: Fíjate en lo que se sumó: 0. ¿Cambió eso al 47 en algo?
Piensa en lo que hace cada propiedad. ¿Cuál trata de que un número siga siendo el mismo?
47 + 0 devuelve 47 sin cambios. Busca la propiedad que lleva el nombre de conservar la identidad de un número.

reviewHighlights.formula: Commutative: a + b = b + a | Associative: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c)
steps: 1. Commutative Property: Order does not change sum or product
2. Associative Property: Grouping does not change sum or product
3. Identity Property: a + 0 = a; a · 1 = a
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Properties of Operations is applying the commutative property where it does not belong, or confusing it with the associative property. Students often assume 15 − 8 = 8 − 15 (it does not: 7 ≠ −7 — commutative only works for addition and multiplication), or they see parentheses move and call it "associative" even when the numbers inside just swapped places, like (2 + 3) + 4 = (3 + 2) + 4 (that is commutative — the order inside the parentheses changed, not the grouping). Before you label a property, ask: did only the order change (commutative), did only the grouping change (associative), or was a 0 or 1 involved (identity)?

level1.stem: Which property lets you rearrange 8 × 5 to 5 × 8?
level1.explanation: Changing the order of factors is the Commutative Property of Multiplication.
choiceFeedback: That property regroups three or more numbers using parentheses. Here there are only two factors and they simply changed places.
Associative groups differently. Commutative rearranges the order.
You rearranged 8 and 5 — that's swapping order, which is Commutative.
hints: The factors 8 and 5 swapped positions. Nothing else changed — no parentheses, no new numbers.
Swapping order is one property; moving parentheses is another. Which happened here?
Compare: 8 × 5 became 5 × 8, like trading seats. Choose the property that lets factors change order.
level1.explanationEs: Cambiar el orden de los factores es la Propiedad Conmutativa de la Multiplicación.
hintsEs: Los factores 8 y 5 cambiaron de posición. Nada más cambió: ni paréntesis ni números nuevos.
Cambiar el orden es una propiedad; mover los paréntesis es otra. ¿Cuál pasó aquí?
Compara: 8 × 5 se volvió 5 × 8, como intercambiar asientos. Elige la propiedad que permite cambiar el orden de los factores.

level3.stem: Which property of operations is shown by the equation (7 + 4) + 6 = 7 + (4 + 6)?
choiceFeedback: Commutative changes the ORDER of the addends. Here 7, 4 and 6 stay in order and only the parentheses move.
Identity adds zero and leaves a number unchanged. No zero appears in this equation.
Distributive spreads a multiplication across a sum. This equation contains no multiplication.
level3.explanation: The addends stay in the order 7, 4, 6 on both sides. Only the grouping changes, which is the associative property. Both sides have a value of 17.

level3.prompt: Explain why the commutative property works for addition and multiplication but NOT for subtraction and division. Give a specific number example for each operation to prove your point.
level3.sentenceFrame: Addition: ___ + ___ = ___ + ___ = ___ (works). Subtraction: ___ − ___ ≠ ___ − ___ because ___. Multiplication: ___ × ___ = ___ × ___ = ___ (works). Division: ___ ÷ ___ ≠ ___ ÷ ___ because ___.
level3.hint: Apply the Distributive Property to expand the expression, showing how the multiplier distributes to each term.
hints: The commutative property claims order doesn't matter. Your job is to show when that claim breaks.
Pick two numbers and run all four operations both ways. Note which give matching results and which don't.
Try 10 and 2: compute 10 − 2 and 2 − 10, then 10 ÷ 2 and 2 ÷ 10. Compare each pair and record what you find.
level3.explanation: Addition and multiplication combine two amounts into a total or a product, and swapping which one you name first does not change that total: 10 + 2 = 2 + 10 = 12 and 10 × 2 = 2 × 10 = 20. Subtraction and division ask 'how much is left' or 'how many fit,' which depends on which number starts: 10 − 2 = 8 but 2 − 10 = −8, and 10 ÷ 2 = 5 but 2 ÷ 10 = 0.2.
level3.explanationEs: La suma y la multiplicación combinan dos cantidades en un total o un producto, y cambiar cuál nombras primero no altera ese resultado: 10 + 2 = 2 + 10 = 12 y 10 × 2 = 2 × 10 = 20. La resta y la división preguntan «cuánto queda» o «cuántos caben», y eso depende de cuál número va primero: 10 − 2 = 8 pero 2 − 10 = −8, y 10 ÷ 2 = 5 pero 2 ÷ 10 = 0.2.
hintsEs: La propiedad conmutativa afirma que el orden no importa. Tu tarea es mostrar cuándo esa afirmación falla.
Escoge dos números y haz las cuatro operaciones en ambos órdenes. Anota cuáles dan resultados iguales y cuáles no.
Prueba con 10 y 2: calcula 10 − 2 y 2 − 10, luego 10 ÷ 2 y 2 ÷ 10. Compara cada par y anota lo que encuentres.
